fatal_errors: The proposed composition-series intervention does not reconstruct the target high-energy ball-milling and spark-plasma-sintering process study.
The cited evidence does not directly demonstrate that atomic-size mismatch is the governing variable independently of grain size, dislocation density, phase constitution, or chemical ordering.
explanation: The hypothesis is scientifically plausible and offers a testable solid-solution-strengthening mechanism, but it addresses a different controlled comparison from the target. The target attributes the measured hardness and compressive strength primarily to the synergy of nanocrystalline Hall–Petch strengthening, milling-induced dislocation density and lattice strain, solid-solution strengthening, densification, and an FCC/BCC phase mixture produced by HEBM and SPS. The generated hypothesis isolates atomic-size mismatch in nominally single-phase alloys and therefore captures only one secondary aspect of the target mechanism. It omits the specified CoCrFeNiTi powder state, milling and SPS windows, nanocrystalline grain refinement, porosity suppression, 83% FCC/17% BCC structure, cast baseline, and quantitative outcomes. Its phase-purity checks and explicit falsification rule provide reasonably good discriminability, although changing composition while holding microstructure genuinely constant may be difficult because atomic-size mismatch itself can alter phase stability, ordering, and grain evolution. Evidence E1 and E3 support solution strengthening or lattice friction only indirectly; E4 is a database rather than direct mechanistic evidence, and E2 is largely irrelevant to the proposed room-temperature comparison.
